title: Exactness of affine K-injective boundaries
statement: Let f:X\to Y be affine and I a K-injective cochain complex of O_X-modules with quasi-coherent cohomology in every integer degree. Write F=g_* for direct image to modules over f_*O_X. For n in Z let h be the left part of the chosen homology data of I.sc n, with differential into cycles h.fprime and class projection h.pi. The short complex F(I^{n-1}) -> F(h.K) -> F(h.H), whose maps are F(h.fprime) and F(h.pi), is exact at its middle object. No epimorphy of its second map, left adjoint or adjunction is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0AVW, proof, canonical cohomology calculation; Tag 08D4, N=1 truncation argument; Tag 08BS, restriction of K-injectives to opens

proof.text: For an affine open V in Y its inverse image U is affine. Restrict the quasi-coherent cohomology modules to U. Affine vanishing, transported from the source H model to module right-derived sections, gives R^p Gamma(U,-)=0 on these modules for p>0. Sections commute with countable products because sections are evaluation of the underlying sheaf, whose limits are computed sectionwise.

Set A=tau_{<=n}I and B=tau_{>=n}A=H^n(I)[-n]. Left exactness of derived sections makes H^n(RGamma(A)) -> H^n(RGamma(I)) invertible, since the upper tail starts in degree n+1. Apply the unbounded bound with N=1 to the lower tail tau_{<=n-1}I. Its derived sections vanish in degrees n and n+1, so the truncation triangle makes H^n(RGamma(A)) -> H^n(RGamma(B)) invertible. The derived single-object identification and the degree-zero right-derived-functor isomorphism identify the latter object with Gamma(U,H^n(I)).

Restriction to U preserves K-injectivity by exact extension by zero and its restriction adjunction (Tag 08BS). Identify the preceding map with the actual cycle-class map. The natural comparison Gamma(K) -> RGamma(QK) is invertible for K=I: compare I to its K-injective resolution; a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence and sections preserve homotopies. Sections preserve kernels, so Gamma(A) -> Gamma(I) induces an isomorphism on H^n. The natural comparison square for A -> I therefore makes Gamma(A) -> RGamma(A) invertible on H^n. In the square for A -> B, Gamma(B) -> RGamma(B) is the canonical bottom-degree identification. The degree-n component of A -> B is the quotient of cycles by boundaries, so commutativity identifies the composite isomorphism with the raw class map. The left homology data is a kernel followed by its cokernel; their uniqueness identifies its pi with that raw map. No arbitrary comparison isomorphism is chosen.

Injectivity of the raw comparison says that a cycle section with zero homology-sheaf class represents zero in the section-complex cohomology, so it is the differential of a degree-(n-1) section. Thus kernel of F(pi) equals image of F(fprime) on every affine open. The other inclusion is differential squared equal to zero. Local exactness on the affine basis is exactness of the displayed module-sheaf short complex. Empty opens, zero complexes and all degrees are included.

theorem affine_algebra_kinjective_boundary_exactness
    {X Y : Scheme.{v}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom f]
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    [I.IsKInjective] (hI : ∀ n : ℤ, (I.homology n).IsQuasicoherent) (n : ℤ) :
    ((ShortComplex.mk (I.sc n).homologyData.left.f' (I.sc n).homologyData.left.π
      (I.sc n).homologyData.left.f'_π).map
        (RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage (toDirectImageAlgebraSpace f))).Exact
